notes:
POC context and SLO alignment notes:
- Business driver: real-time conversational assistants for traders and support agents. High priority on perceived latency (end-user) + regulatory auditability.
- Throughput target: baseline 400 req/s sustained with burst to 1k req/s. Aim to stabilize p95 non-streaming <= 250ms, p50 ~ 60-80ms. Streaming sessions: perceived token latency p95 <= 350-450ms depending on chunking; p99 target <= 1s.
- POC scope: run both streaming (chunked token streaming over SSE/ws) and non-streaming (single response) workloads, measure both client-side and server-side timings.
- Measurement alignment requirements (customer asks):
  * Client-side timing = time between user send & final UI render (includes network, TLS handshake, first-byte + last-byte). Customer will use RUM probes from EU & NA offices.
  * Server-side timing = Redwood middleware entry-to-last-byte-out. Must provide histogram snapshots (p50/p95/p99) and raw latency buckets.
  * Streaming nuance: define events - first-token-latency (FTL), inter-token-90th, final-chunk-latency. For streaming SLOs they want FTL p95 <= 200ms and inter-token p95 <= 120ms for 90% of sessions.
  * Cold vs warm starts: capture cold-start tags (model cache misses, VM spin-up). SLO baseline excludes cold start windows but P99 SLA needs crediting approach for cold-start incidents.
  * Batching & KV cache effects: measured p95 must be reported both with batching enabled (to demonstrate cost profile) and disabled (to demonstrate raw request latency). KV cache hit-rate will be logged and correlated with tail latency.
  * Measurement windows: 1m, 5m, 1h aggregations; SLO reporting weekly/monthly. Need sliding-window p99 calculations and incident thresholds.
- Instrumentation ask: request/response IDs (trace-id), per-request kernel-selection tag, queueing_time, execution_time, network_rtt estimate. Agent wants client/server timestamp alignment (NTP skew allowance) - we'll include offset headers.
- SLA negotiation points outstanding: crediting model for p99 breaches (how many minutes of p99 > threshold triggers credit), definition of what counts as force-majeure (regional infra outage vs maintenance), and capacity resourcing (guaranteed reserved GPU pool vs soft burst).
- Cost sensitivity: target 25-30% lower unit cost vs internal managed endpoints to justify migration. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization) but need quality regressions tracked via evals.
- Quotes from stakeholders: "Perceived latency is what the traders notice — we need end-to-end numbers, not just server logs." — Head of Trading Apps.
- Internal notes: timeline tight - want production cutover H2 2026 if POC meets SLOs. Prioritize SLO measurement spec before POC kickoff.
- Links: pricing deck & security FAQ in drive; RG ticket RDW-3421 for initial perf tests.
summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on dedicated capacity with explicit SLO measurement alignment. Customer needs clear separation and mapping between client-side perceived latency and server-side metrics, detailed streaming SLOs, and contractual language for p99 tail credits. POC scheduled to validate throughput/latency and prove cost delta vs internal infra.
